name: Sporgout

notes.languages: Can't speak, Speak with plants, Telepathy 100 feet (infected creatures only)

spells.name: Dominate (Mycosome-Infected creatures only)
spells.text:
You take command of the target, forcing it to obey your orders. If you issue an obviously self-destructive order, the target doesn't act until you issue a new order. The effect depends on its Will save.

---

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is Stunned 1 as it fights off your commands.

Failure You control the target. It gains the Controlled condition, but it can attempt a Will save at the end of each of its turns. On a success, the spell ends.

Critical Failure As a failure, but the target receives a new save only if you give it a new order that is against its nature, such as killing its allies.

---

Heightened (10th) The duration is unlimited.

spells.name: Lignify
spells.text:
You turn the target's flesh slowly into wood. The target must attempt a Fortitude save. Creatures with the plant trait have a +2 circumstance bonus to saves against this spell.

---

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is Slowed 1 for 1 round.

Failure The target is slowed 1 and must attempt a Fortitude save at the end of each of its turns; this ongoing save has the incapacitation trait. On a failed save, the slowed condition increases by 1 (or 2 on a critical failure). A successful save reduces the slowed condition by 1. When a creature is unable to act due to the slowed condition from lignify, the creature is permanently non-magically petrified, though it's turned to wood instead of stone. The spell ends if the creature is magically petrified or the slowed condition is removed.

Critical Failure As failure, but the target is initially Slowed 2.

spells.name: Speak with Plants (Constant)
spells.text:
You can ask questions of and receive answers from plants and fungi, but the spell doesn't make them more friendly or intelligent than normal. Most normal plants and fungi have a distinctive view of the world around them, so they don't recognize details about creatures or know anything about the world beyond their immediate vicinity. Cunning plant or fungus monsters are likely to be terse and evasive, while less intelligent ones often make inane comments.

---

Heightened (4th) The duration is 8 hours.

spells.name: One with Plants
spells.text:
You can either transform into a plant or merge with plant matter. While transformed, you can't move or affect anything outside the plant, but you can cast spells as long as they don't require line of effect beyond the plant. You can Dismiss this spell.

- Merge with Plants The spell's duration is 10 minutes. While casting the spell, you must touch a plant with enough volume to fit you and your possessions or the spell is disrupted. While merged, you can hear, but not see, what's going on outside the plant. If the plant takes damage while you're inside it, you're expelled from the plant and take 10d6 damage. Magic passage expels you without dealing damage. The spell ends if you're ever outside the plant.

- Turn into a Plant The spell's duration is 8 hours. You become a Large plant—typically a tree. Perception checks don't reveal your true nature, but a successful Nature or Survival check against your spell DC reveals that you appear to be a plant that is strangely new to the area. While in this form, you can observe everything around you, using your normal senses. As a plant, your AC is 20, and only status bonuses, status penalties, circumstance bonuses, and circumstance penalties affect you. Any successes and critical successes you roll on Reflex saves are failures

spells.name: Vanishing Tracks
spells.text:
You obscure the tracks you leave behind. The DC of checks to Track you gains a +4 status bonus or is equal to your spell DC, whichever results in a higher DC.

---
Heightened (2nd) The duration increases to 8 hours.

Heightened (4th) The duration increases to 8 hours. The spell has a range of 20 feet and targets up to 10 creatures.

items.name: Sporesense
items.text: The sporgout can detect mycosome-infected creatures as a precise sense within the listed range.

items.name: Hidden Roots
items.text:
Trigger A creature within the sporgout's reach uses a move action or leaves a square during a move action it's using

---
Effect The sporgout infects the triggering creature with their mycosomes, then attempts to trip it.

items.name: Shimmer Spores
items.text: 30 feet. The sporgout constantly disperses mind-addling spores. A creature that enters or begins their turn in the emanation becomes Confused for 1 round unless it succeeds at a DC 31 Will save save. Regardless of the result, the creature is temporarily immune for 1 minute unless it later becomes infected with mycosomes, at which point it must save against shimmer spores again the next time it enters the emanation.

foundry.level: aura, illusion, mental, plant, poison, primal

items.name: Fungal Decomposition
items.text: The sporgout activates the spores inside a mycosome-infected creature within 60 feet, dealing 4d12 poison damage (DC 34 basic Fortitude save save). On a successful save, the creature is no longer infected.

items.name: Mycosomes
items.text: A creature hit by a sporgout's Strikes is infected with their fungal mycosomes for 1 minute if it isn't already. Infected creatures are more susceptible to some of the sporgout's abilities. An infected creature is considered infected by all sporgouts. This is a poison effect.

items.name: Sneak Attack
items.text: The sporgout's Strikes deal an additional 1d6 precision damage to Off-Guard creatures.

text:
Countless myths warn about the dangers of stepping into a ring of mushrooms, but few extend this caution to the hidden threat that often lurks beneath them. Sporgouts are born when mushroom colonies aiding in the decay of a corpse consume vast amounts of primal energy, whether because the body was a being of primal magic (like a leshy or arboreal) or because it died in an area of strong fey influence. These colonies become so infused with magic that they attain their own sentience as a singular sporgout, lying in wait underground to ambush those who carelessly draw near. Though once believed to be undead, sporgouts are not reanimated corpses; while they absorb the nutrients and magic of their host body, they are wholly new creatures.

Sporgouts resemble unnatural humanoids with bodies like rotting logs or burned or petrified wood, covered in a colorful riot of strange fungi and lichens. They have no eyes or mouths, though they turn their heads as if mimicking beings who use such features to communicate. They have little interest in interacting with strangers and are often mistaken for solitary creatures, but like mundane mushrooms, sporgouts can and do communicate with each other across long distances through a mycorrhizal network.
